The Regional Council Act defines the powers, functions and responsibilities of the Chittagong Hill Tracts Regional Council. The Land Commission Act provides for the expeditious resolution of land-related disputes in the Chittagong Hill Tracts (in short, CHT) by a specially constituted Commission. However, all those statutes duly take into cognizance the "customs" of the circle/district region and of its tribes. He also goes to argue that the Chittagong Hill Tracts Regulations, 1900, which is one of the major legal instruments for the administration of the hill region, has expressly recognized the prevalence of the customary laws of the Chittagong Hill Tracts. XIX, XX and XXI of 1989 he submits that vide the said statutes the disputes between the members of the tribes of the concerned district are to be tried and disposed of as per the “প্রচলিত রীতি-নীতি অনুযায়ী" by the local Karbaries, Headmen and Chiefs of the respective mouza and circle concerned, with provision for appeal before the Divisional Commissioner, who is obliged to consult 3(three) experts from the tribe concerned while hearing appeals. Similarly, section 6(1)(Kha) of the Chittagong Hill Tracts Land Disputes Resolution Commission Act, 2001 provides that the Commission will resolve land related disputes in accordance with the "পার্বত্য চট্টগ্রামের প্রচলিত রীতি-নীতি অনুযায়ী"।

In this regard, he goes to argue that prior to issuance of succession certificates, the Deputy Commissioner of each hill district, directly or through the Upazilla Nirbahi Officers and Assistant Commissioner (Land) used to consult the concerned Mouza Headmen on the identities of the heirs and successors of any landed estate situated within the district concern, which indicates the prevalence of customary law of different tribes of the CHT recognizing the role of the traditional institutions, regarding matters of succession.

43. He further submits that application of Hindu-Dayabhaga Law by the respondent No. 2 referring to the ratio as decided in Karatala L Bihar vs HR Chowdhury, 40 DLR (AD) (1988)137, on the court that the Appellate Division has held that said principles would apply to the Buddhists of Bangladesh, is a misconceived one, for the said case involved a suit for declaration of title and confirmation or alternatively, recovery of possession, and also for a declaration on the illegality of a "Nirupannama", devolving an estate of the Chief Priest of Lakshmi Bihar, who was a member of Barua Buddhist (Bengali) community of Chittagong district and not members of any non-Bengali ethnic groups, including the Marma, Rakhine, Chakma, Tanchangya, etc.; as were the other contenders; however, in the said case the respective contending parties did not contest the application of Hindu Dayabhaga Law to them. As such, he submits that ratio of 40 DLR (AD) 137 cannot be regarded as a yardstick to establish that Hindu Dayabhaga Law would apply to each and every case of inheritance concerning Buddhists of Bangladesh, and certainly not to Buddhists who are ethnically different from the Buddists (Bengali) Barua community such as, the petitioners Nos. 1-8 and respondent Nos. 9-13 in the present case.

44. He also submits that in a number of cases the Appellate Division has categorically upheld the application of tribal customary law, rather than Hindu law; like in AS Prue Chowdhury vs KS Prue Chowdhury, 6 BLT (AD) (1998) 109 = 50 DLR (AD) 73, the Appellate Division while resolving the issue held that the office of the Bohmong Chief is a customary office and both the government and the Court have to recognize the custom and not to introduce any other criterion or factor which will add to the customary requirements of that office. Also, in Rajkumari Unika Devi vs Bangladesh, 12 BLT (AD) (2004), 141 = 9 BLC (AD) 181. the Appellate Division observed, inter-alia, that the appointment was valid, since it followed the "custom, usage and tradition of the Mong Circle."

45. In the case of Chakmas and Tripuras too, he goes to argue that it is customary law that applies, and the religious affiliation of the Chakmas or Tripuras is not considered, as supported in Chakma Byaktigoto Paribarik Am pp 84-85, and Trzura Byaktigoto Paribarik Am, pp 67). Referring to another publication on Chakma Inheritance Law by Bankim Krishna Dewan (Chakma Jatiyo Bichar Poddhoti O Chakma Uttoradhikar Protha, Rangamati, 1985) he goes to contend that it contains several summaries of case laws from the Courts of the Chakma Chief, the Deputy Commissioner, the Divisional Commissioner, the Board of Appeal and the Provincial Governor, in which customary law, and not any law of religious affiliation, including Hindu Law, were applied.

46. Accordingly, he submits that the laws and practices prevailing in Bangladesh clearly indicate that inheritance and other personal law matters of the different ethno-linguistic-cultural groups that are not ethno-linguistically "Bengali are governed by the laws of the tribe/people concerned, irrespective of their religious affiliation. In the stated circumstances, he submits that the observations of the Appellate Division in Karatala L Bihar vs HR Chowdhury, 40 DLR (AD) (1988) 137 must be confined to the circumstances of the case, involving Bengali Buddhists (Baruas) and involving litigants, whose views on the application of Hindu Dayabhaga Law cannot be impugned to apply to other Buddhists, and definitely not to the non-Bengali Buddhist communities. Consequently, he submits that the respondent No. 2 ought to have referred the matter in dispute to the concerned Circle Chief and/or Mouza Headman, or at least should have consulted them prior to deciding upon the matter.

47. The cardinal issue which requires determination in the present Rules Nisi is whether dispute over succession within Marma community, who are ethnically non-Bengali Buddhists, should be resolved in accordance with Hindu Dayabhaga Law or with the 'social customs" of the said community of the Chittagong Hill Tracts (in short, CHT).

48. The property in question i.e., 24.30 acres of land is situated within Khagrachari Hill District, one of the 3(three) Hill Districts of the Chittagong Hill Tracts. It is, however, the emphatic contention of the Intervenor as well the petitioners of writ petition No.3285 of 2009 that the applicability of law regarding succession differs depending upon the religious affiliation, ethnicity and place of residence. Thus, the law applicable to persons of Buddhist affiliation will go to differ depending upon their ethnicity (whether Bengali or Non-Bengali), and that if the latter, depending upon the tribe to which they belong and the district where they are located.

49. It has also been contended that the application of Hindu Law (whether Dayabhaga or Mitakshara of otherwise) to Buddhists of Bangladesh is limited to members of the Barua community, who are Buddhists by affiliation, who generally regard themselves as ethnically Bengali and quite distinct from the non-Bengali Buddhists from different ethnic groups such as, the Chakma, Marma, Tanchangya and Rakhine who reside in the Chittagong Hill Tracts and in several plains districts of the country.

50. Further, it has been contended that "social custom" has been recognised by the Constitution of the country having the force of law and that the Regulations, 1900 has duly recognised its applicability in the matters of personal law of the respective tribes of all the 3(three) districts of the Chittagong Hill Tracts where consultation with the local Headmen and Circle Chiefs of the respective Mouza has been made obligatory. In the said backdrop, when both the contending parties of the case pleaded to resolve the dispute applying “প্রচলিত নিয়মে”, as such, disposing of the suits by the respondent No. 2 applying Hindu Dayabhaga Law on the plea that the Appellate Division in the case reported in 40 DLR (AD) 137 has made the principles of the said school applicable in matters of succession of Buddhists belonging to Marma Community, cannot be tenable in the eye of law.

51. The word "law" has been defined in our Constitution vide Article 152, which provides as under:

"Law" means any Act, ordinance, order rule regulation, bye-law, notification or other legal instrument, and any custom or usage, having the force of law in Bangladesh; "

52. The Chittagong Hill Tracts Regulations, 1900 (in short, the Regulations) recognizes "social customs" in the area concern along with the authority of the 3(three) traditional Circle Chiefs and about 380 mouza Headmen. In this regard the relevant provisions of law may be looked into, which are quoted herein below:

"Section 8

(1)  .............................

(2)   .............................

(3)   .............................

(4) The Joint District Judge as a court of original jurisdiction, shall try all civil cases in accordance with the existing laws, customs and usages of the districts concerned except the cases arising out of the family laws and other customary laws of the tribes of the districts of Rangamati, Khagrachari and Band arban respectively which shall be triable by the Mauza Headmen and Circle Chiefs."

53. However, vide regulation 35 of the Regulations, 1900 the districts of Chittagong Hill Tracts comprises the Circles of the three Chiefs, viz the Chakma Chief, the Bohmong Chief and Mong Chief.

54. In this regard, regulation 38 provides as under:

"38. The Circle-Chiefs shall form an Advisory Council to the Deputy Commissioner, and shall assist him with information and advise on all matters which concerned the administration of their respective circles, and shall exercise their authority as Chiefs in the prompt enforcement in the mauzas of their circles of all orders of the Deputy Commissioner".

55. Regulation 39 enumerates the prerogatives of the Circle Chief to be consulted with on matters affecting the administration of the CHT, which runs as follows:

"39. The Deputy Commissioner shall consult the Chiefs on important matters affecting the administration of the CHT. For this purpose a conference shall be held, at least twice a year, under the presidency of the Deputy Commissioner, to which the Chiefs or their representatives shall be invited. "

56. Moreover, section 66 of the "খাগড়াছড়ি পার্বত্য জেলা পরিষদ আিইন" (Act No. XX of 1989)" also provides as under:

৬৬।(১) খাগড়াছড়ি পার্বত্য জেলার বাসিন্দা এমন উপজাতীয়গণের মধ্যে কোন সামাজিক,সাংস্কৃতিক বা উপজাতীয় । বিষয়ে বিরোধ দেখা দিলে বিরোধটি নিষ্পত্তির জন্য স্থানীয় কার্বারী বা হেডম্যানের নিকট উত্থাপন করিতে হইবে এবং তিনি সংশ্লিষ্ট উপজাতীয়গণের মধ্যে রীতি-নীতি অনুযায়ী বিরোধের নিষ্পত্তি

করিবেন।

(2)

(৩)

57. From the above quoted provisions of law it is rather evident that considering the role of "social customs" being played in all spheres of the respective tribes of the 3(three) districts of CHT the legislature has duly given recognition to it having the force of law.

58. However, in a number of cases the Appellate Division as well has categorically upheld the applications of triable customary law, as referred and relied upon by the Intervenor.

59. In AS Prue Chowdhury vs KS Prue Chowdhury, 6 BLT (AD) (1998) 109 = 50 DLR (AD) 73, the appellant who was a member of the Marma community of Bandarban hill district had challenged the decision of the Government in appointing and recognizing another member of his family as the Chief of the Bohmong Circle of the CHT (thereby not appointing and recognizing him to the office) on the ground, inter-alia, that this appointment was made in violation of the age-old usage, traditions and customs of the Bobmong Chiefs family.

60. The Appellate Division while declaring the appointment of the government of the respondent as Bohmong Chief to be ultra vires observed, inter-alia, that, "The court will only inquire whether the selection has been made following the tradition, custom and usage which govern such selection Government will also not deny that the susceptibilities of the people should not be ignored. "

61. In Rajkumari Unika Devi vs Bangladesh, 12 BLT (AD) (2004), 141 = 9 BLC (AD) 181, the appellant had challenged the decision of the Government in appointing and recognizing another member of her family as the Chief of the Mong Circle of the CHT (thereby not appointing and recognizing her to the office) alleging, inter-alia, that this was done in violation of the age-old usage, traditions and customs of the Mong Circle. In the said case the Appellate Division observed, inter-alia,"

"Customs play a predominant part in the matter of succession in the absence of any heir to the late Mong Chief Customs in this case is the social customs of the Mong Chief which constitutes a source of law for the Mong Circle in the absence of any law as regards succession. The customs is something that has the effect of local law."

62. From the above, it is apparent that the statute as well as the dictum as settled by the Appellate Division in a number of cases have duly recognized applicability of the "social customary law" in the case of succession together with the cancellation of the Circle Chief for the respective community of the Chittagong Hill Tracts.

63. As for the instant case, the respondent Nos. 7 and 8, 2(two) sons of Akra Mogini, who was one of the 3(three) daughters of Abetu Mogini, one of the daughters of late Dugya Mog, (the owner of 24.30 acres of land) instituted Civil Suit No. 20 of 1992 impleading the respective defendants who were the daughters and sons of Krayari Mogini and Pusuma Mogini, before the Deputy Commissioner, Khagrachari and ex-officio Civil Judge, the respondent No. 2 , on 9-6-1991(Annexure-C) contending, inter alia,

“প্রচলিত বিধির নিয়মে আওয়া মগিনী ওয়ারিশান সনদপত্র মূলে কোন সম্পত্তি অংশীদার বা দাবীদার হিসাবে যোগ্য বা প্রযোজ্য নহে বলিয়া মনে করি। তাই অনিয়মিত ওয়ারিশানের মামলার নথি তলব করিয়া বিজ্ঞ আদালতে পর্যালোচনা ক্রমে প্রচলিত নিয়মে এবং স্থানীয় হেডম্যানের পুনঃতদস্ত প্রতিবেদন তলবে সাক্ষীর শুনানী ��্রহনপূর্বক অনিয়মিত ইস্যুকৃত একক উত্তারাধিকারী সনদপত্র বাতিল করিয়া অধীনগণের প্রকৃত

ওয়ারিশান হিসাবে ইস্মুকৃত উত্তারিধারী সনদপত্র বহাল রাখার আকুল আবেদন করিতেছি” ।

and prayed for—

“মৃত দুগ্য মগের প্রকৃত ওয়ারিশান সত্ত্ব প্রচলিত নিয়মে বিজ্ঞ আদালত কর্তৃক নির্ধরিণ করিয়া পূর্বে অনিয়মিত ওয়ারিশান পত্র বাতিল পূর্বক নিম্ন তফশীলভূক্ত জমি ছক মতে ভাগবন্টন করিয়া পৃথকখতিয়ানে এর ডিক্রি প্রদানে মহোদয়ের চির আজ্ঞা হয়।”

64. The defendant Nos. 1-10 entered appearance by filing written statement on 14-10-1992 contending inter alia, that the dispute in question involved the inheritance of Marma community of Khagrachari Hill District (legally termed as tribal dispute) and thus, made a prayer for:—

“অতএব হুজুব আদালত দয়া পরবশ হয়ে সরেজমিনে বিচার বিভাগীয় তদন্তক্রমে নালিশী ভূমি ওয়ারিশানের মধ্যে মগ সম্প্রদায়ের ক্ষেত্রে প্রযোজ্য আইন অনুযায়ী ভাগ বন্টনের ডিক্রি দানের বিহিত অজ্ঞা হয়।”

65. Hence, it is apparent that the pleadings of both the contending parties was to resolve the issue applying "প্রচলিত নিয়মে", social customs, as is applicable for Marma community.

66. However, after filing of the said suit, pursuant to Memo dated 21-3-1992 issued earlier by the respondent No. 2 the concerned

Headmen of the respective Mouza had made a request to the said respondent to keep further proceedings suspended for proper inquiry con-tending, inter alia-

“.............নিম্নস্বাক্ষরকারী এবং উপস্থিত মারমা সম্প্রদায়ী গণমান্য ব্যক্তিবর্গণণ বুঝিতে পারিতেছেন না। কারণ সকলে উপস্থিত সুষ্ঠু তদন্ত করা না হইলে পূর্বের মত ভুল হইয়া বিভিন্ন জটিলতার সৃষ্টি হইবে বা হইতে পারে বিধায় প্রচলিত কাষ্টমারী বা সামাজিক বিধি মতে মৃত দগ্য মগের প্রকৃত ওয়ারিশান পুনঃ তদন্ত মোতাবেক সর্বশেষ সুষ্ঠু তদন্তের সাপেক্ষে মারমা সম্প্রদায় বহু গন্যমান্য ব্যক্তির উপস্থিতে সমন্বয়ে নিধারণের জন্য মহোদয়ের নিকট পুনঃ এক মাসের সময়ের প্রার্থনা করিতেছি। অনুরূপভাবে পূর্বের সকল বিবিধ মামলা মূলে মৃত ব্যক্তির দুগ্য কার্যক্রম কিংবা সংশ্লিষ্ট সম্পত্তি বিষয়ে যে কোন কার্যক্রম মহোদয়ের পরবর্তী আদেশ না হওয়া স্থগিত রাখার একাস্ত আবেদন”।

67. However in the inquiry report dated 22-2-1993 the Thana Nirbahi Officer, Khagrachari, Police-Khagrachari pursuant to Memo dated 6-12-2009 (Annexure-D) stated, inter alia—,

68. Subsequently, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) Khagrachari passed an order on 11-9-1993 in the form of recommendation for consideration by the respondent No. 2. ultimately, the Deputy Commissioner and the ex-officio Civil Judge, the respondent No. 2 vide the impugned judgment and order dated 22-9-1996(Annexure-A) has disposed of the suit observing, inter alia

“সম্পত্তি বিতরণের আইন সম্পর্কে ২ পক্ষের ভিন্ন দাবীঃ বিবাদীপক্ষ দাবী করিয়াছে যে, আমাদের উত্তরাধিকারের কোন লিখিত আইন না থাকায় স্থানীয় প্রথা মতে মৃত দুগ্য মগের সম্পত্তি তাহার ওয়ারিশদের মধ্যে ভাগ করিতে হইবে । বাদী পক্ষ অবশ্য এই দাবী অস্বীকার করিয়া হিন্দু দয়াভাগা আইন অনুসারে সম্পত্তিভাগের দাবী জানাইয়াছি। সেই বিষয়ে ভিন্ন ভিন্ন লেখকের লেখা হইতে ইহা জানা যায় যে, উত্তরাধিকারের ক্ষেত্রে হিন্দু দয়াভাগা আইন বৌদ্ধ ধর্মাবলম্বীদের ক্ষেত্রে প্রযোজ্য। ৪০ ডিএলজার এ রিপোর্টকৃত অমৃত নন্দ মহাথেরো বনাম হৃদয় রন চৌধুরীর মামলার রায় হইতে ইহা প্রতীয়মান হয় যে, বাংলাদেশের বৌদ্ধদের উত্তরাধিকারের ক্ষেত্রে হিন্দু দায়ভাগা প্রযোজ্য । মামলার অবশ্য উভয় পক্ষ উত্তরাধিকারের ক্ষেত্রে হিন্দু দায়ভাগা আইন প্রযোজ্য কিনা সে বিষয়ের বিস্তারিত আলোচনা করেন নাই । বৌদ্ধ ধমবিলম্বীদের ক্ষেত্রে হিন্দু দায়ভাগা আইন প্রযোজ্য বলিয়া উল্লিখিত মামলার উভয়পক্ষ এবং মানীয় বিচারপতিগণ কর্তৃক মানিয়া নেওয়ার ঘটনা ও সংশ্লিষ্ট বিষয়ে বিশেষজ্ঞদের লেখা পুস্তকে প্রদত্ত মতামত হইতে ইহা ধরিয়া নেয়া যায় যে, হিন্দু দায়ভাগা আইনই বৌদ্ধ ধর্মবিলম্বীদের জন্য প্রযোজ্য হইবে । ৩২ ডিএলআর এ রিপোর্টকৃত অজিতা ভিক্ষু বনাম অগ্র বংশ মহাথেরো মামলায় বৌদ্ধ ধর্মবিলম্বীদের ক্ষেত্রে হিন্দু আইন প্রযোজ্য নয় বলিয়া মাননীয় বিচারপতিগণ যে মতামত দিয়াছেন ৪০ ডিএলআর এ রিপোর্টকৃত উল্লিখিত মামলার বিচারকারী মাননীয় বিচারপতিগণ উহাকে সুইপিং বলিয়া আখ্যায়িত করার বিষয়টি উপরোক্ত মতামতকে আরও দৃঢ় করিয়াছে। সুতরাং সিদ্ধান্ত নেওয়া যায় যে, মারমাদের উত্তরাধিকার নির্ণয়ের ক্ষেত্রে হিন্দু দায়াভাগা আইন প্রযোজ্য হইবে।”

69. In other words, the concerned Court applied the principles of Hindu Dayabhaga Law to the Buddhists of the Marma community firstly, on the alleged claim of the plaintiffs, (the respondent Nos.7 and 8) and secondly, applying the ratio of the case reported in 40 DLR (AD) 137 and thereby had cancelled the 3(three) Miscellaneous Cases bearing Nos.110, 65 and 98 all of 1990. Vide the said order he further can-celled the claim of the respondent No.6 to get 8.10 acres of land upon dismissing his suit and also observed that his brother in law, Abrechai Marma, who is the petitioner No.1 in writ petition No. 3285 of 2009, not being an heir would not get any portion of the property in question and accordingly, had directed the concerned Upazilla Nirbahi Officer for recovery of posses-sion from the petitioner No.1 and others who were not the successive heirs, within 60 (sixty) days.

70. The findings of the respondent No. 2 has also been mandated as lawful by the appellate authority in Civil Appeal (Khagrachari) Case No. 84 of 1992, so preferred by the defendant No.8, the petitioner of writ petition No.2829 of 2006, the only son of Kraynori Mogini, who also filed separate application claiming to get entire share of his mother in total 8.10 acres and that both the applications of respondent Nos. 6, 7 and 8 were disposed of vide the impugned judgment and order passed by the Land Appeal Board (Khagrachari) Case No. 4-27 of 2001 (Appeal), upholding the findings of the respondent No. 2.

71. As has been observed earlier, the impugned judgment and order dated 22-9-1996 has been passed by the respondent No. 2 applying the principles of Hindu Dayabhaga Law for succession of Buddhists, (the petitioners and respondent Nos. 9-13) who belong to Marma community relying on the claim of the plaintiffs (the respondent Nos.7 and 8); whereas from the plaint it is rather evident that they had claimed to apply "social customs" to resolve the dispute in question. Hence, the said findings of the respondent No.2 have no leg stand, for having been passed beyond the pleadings.

72. Secondly, the said respondent has applied the rationale of the case reported in 40 DLR (AD) 137 for application of the principles Hindu Dayabhaga Law. It is fact that the Appellate Division in the said case has applied the principles of the said school where the contending parties belonged to the Buddhist (Bengali) Barua community (who are not the members of any non-Bengali ethnic groups including Marma, Takhaine, Chakma, Tanchangya, etc.) over the issue of declaration of title and confirmation, alternatively for recovery of possession; but the fact remains that they are the respective parties who did not dispute application of Hindu Dayabhaga Law; as such, the findings of the Appellant Division should be confined to the facts of the said case and cannot be the ratio decidendi in the instant ease where both the parties had pleaded to apply "social customs", not Hindu Dayabhaga Law. Moreover, in a number of cases the Appellate-Division has duly upheld the application of tribal customary law in the matter of succession of Buddhists by religious affiliation. In addition, the categorical assertion of the petitioners as well as the Intervenor is that customary law applies in the case of succession of Marma community of CHT, which has not been refuted by the respondents concerned in their affidavit in opposition with supporting documents.

73. Moreover, before passing the impugned judgment and order dated 22-9-1996 by the respondent No.2, from Annexure-C (the prayer of the local Headman to re-inquire) it appears that the opinion was sought from the concerned Headman of the respective Mouza in compliance of the requirement as prescribed under the Regulations, 1900, but while passing the impugned judgment and order by the said respondent it does not reflect that the opinion of the concern Headman was actually considered.

74. Lastly, before parting with the judgment it is pertinent to remember one important fact that the property in question has devolved upon the respective contending parties through the maternal line.

75. In view of the above facts, circumstances, observations and findings we have no manner of doubt to final that disposing of the respective suits by the respondent No. 2 applying Hindu Dayabhaga Law in the case of succession of Marma community of the Chittagong Hill Tracts basing on the alleged claim of the respondent Nos. 7 and 8 and the ratio as decided in 40 DLR (AD) 137, is without any lawful authority having no mandate of law.

76. In the result, both the Rules in connection with Writ Petition Nos. 3285 of 2009 and 2829 of 2006 are made absolute.

<u>77. The impugned judgment and order dated 22-9-1996 (Annexure-A) passed by the respondent No. 2, the Deputy Commissioner Khagrachari and the ex-officio Civil Judge in connection with Civil Suit No. 20 of 1992 as well as the judgment and order dated 12-3-2001 passed by the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong Division, Chittagong, respondent No. 4 in Civil Appeal (Khagrachari) Case No. 84 of 1997 (Annexure-C), as has been upheld up to the Land Appeal Board, Dhaka directing vide order dated 12-3-2006 to make portion of 24.30 acres of land and opening a separate Khatian in Volume 6, page 81 by the respondent No. 5 in favour of the respondent Nos. 9-13 pursuant to Namjari Case No. 165 of 1997 (Annexure-B) are hereby declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and hence, are of no legal effect. 78. Since admittedly there is no written law of succession of Marma community hence, the respondent No. 2 is hereby directed to resolve the issue in question afresh on the basis of the pleadings of both the contending parties and other relevant documents and in particular upon consultation with the respective Circle Chief and Headman, as has been envisaged in the Chittagong Hill Tracts Regulations, 1900 preferably within a period of 4(four) months from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment and order.</u>

<u>There will be no order as to costs.</u>

End.

parties:
Nurul Islam (Md) and others------Plaintiff-Appellants
vs
Government of Bangladesh, represented by its Secretary, Ministry of Communication, Dhaka and others Defendant------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal J : This First Appeal is directed against the impugned judgment and decree dated 28-10-2014 (decree signed on 30- 10-2014) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka, in Money Sail No. 79 of 2013 rejecting the plaint.

2. Facts of the case, briefly, are that the appellants herein as plaintiffs brought the aforesaid Money Suit No. 79 of 2013 against the defendant-respondents in the Court of joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka praying the following reliefs:

(ক) উক্ত বাদীগণের উক্ত বিবাদীগণের নিকট ক্ষতিপূরণের পাওনা ১০,৯৫,৬১,০৯৪ টাকা অত্র বাদীগনকে পরিশোধ করিতে অত্র বাদীগনেৱ অনুকূলে অত্র বিবাদীগণের বিরুদ্ধে রায় ও ডিক্রি দিতে আজ্ঞা হয়।

(খ) বাদীগণের পাওনা ১০,৯৫,৬১,০৯৪ (দশ কোটি পঁচানব্বই লক্ষ একষট্টি হাজার চুরানব্বই) টাকা উক্ত বাদীগণকে পরিশোধ করার জন্য নির্দিষ্ট সময়ের মধ্যে বিবাদীগণকে যথাবিহীত নির্দেশ প্রদান করিতে আজ্ঞা হয় ৷

(গ) বাদীগণ আইন ও ইকুইটি মতে আর যে যে প্রতিকার ভাজন হয় তাহাও বাদীগণেৱ অনুকূলে ও অত্র বিবাদীগণের প্রতিকূলে আদেশ ডিক্রি দিতে আজ্ঞা হয় ৷

(ঘ) মামলার যাবতীয় ব্যয় তার বাদীগণেৱ অনুকূলে অত্র বিৰাদীগণের প্রতিকূলে আদেশ, রায় ও ডিক্রি দিতে আজ্ঞা হয় ৷

3. Defendant-respondent Nos.1-9 entered appearance in the suit and filed written statement on 16-4-2014 denying all the material allegations of the plaint contending, inter-alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and manner and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. Therefore, while the suit was in progress the defendant-respondents filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint on the ground that the plaintiffs without referring the matter/dispute to Arbitration Counsel for setting the dispute between the parties as per Clause 25 of the agreement/contract filed the suit on 17-9-2014 and, as such„ the suit is impliedly barred by section 7 of the Arbitration Act.

4. The trial Court after hearing the parties by the impugned judgment and decree dated 28-10-2014 rejected the plaint.

5. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned judgment and decree dated 28-10-2014, the plaintiff-appellants preferred this appeal.

6. Mr Md Aminul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-appellants submits that the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka erred in law in allowing the prayer for rejection of the plaint without properly considering the facts of the case and the case made out by the plaintiff-appellants and the same has occasioned failure of justice. Mr. Aminul Islam further submits that the learned Joint District Judge failed to take into consideration the provision of section 10 of the Arbitration Act, 2010 which clearly provides that if an arbitration agreement exists, any party to such agreement may, at any time before filing a written statement, apply to the Court before which the case is pending to refer the matter to arbitration and it is on record that in this case the defendants without filing any such application to refer the matter to arbitration filed written statement on 16-4-2014 and thereby committed illegality in allowing the application for rejection of the plaint.

7. Drawing our attention to clause 25 of the agreement Mr Aminul Islam submits that admittedly after completion of the construction/development work under agreement the plaintiff-appellants filed the instant money suit claiming compensation amounting to Taka 10, 95,61,094 which does not fall within the ambit of said clause inasmuch as clause 25 of the agreement does not disclose anything with regard to payment of damage or compensation after completion of the construction/development work. Finally, Mr Aminul Islam submits that the defendants' application under Order VII, Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure was Incompetent and misconceived mainly on 2 counts that (i) the subject matter of the present suit and earlier Writ Petition No. 2871 of 2010 are totally distinct in nature and (ii) admittedly the defendant respondents filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure after filing written statement which is contrary to the provision of section 10 of the Arbitration Act. Mr. Md. Aminul Islam in support of his submissions has relied on the decisions reported in 31 DLR (AD) 139, 63 DLR 504 and 43 DLR 286.

8. Mr. SM Zahurul Islam, the learned Advocate; appearing for the respondent No. 2, supports the impugned judgment, which was according to him just, correct and proper.

9. Mr. Bikash Paul, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-respondent No. 7, on the other hand, supports the Impugned judgment and decree and contends that the learned Joint District Judge was perfectly y justified in allowing the prayer for rejection of the plaint on the clear finding that the plaintiffs without referring the dispute to arbitration as per Clause 25 of the agreement filed the suit and earlier the plaintiffs on the similar type dispute filed writ petition and as per direction given in the writ petition the defendants paid all outstanding dues to the plaintiffs. He further submits that the contents of clause 25 of the agreement clearly disclosed that all disputes including financial matter should be referred to arbitration and in that view of the matter the plaintiffs ought to have referred the dispute to arbitration as per clause 25 of the agreement before filing of the instant suit. He further submits that the defendants as per direction given in writ petition paid entire outstanding dues to the plaintiffs and in that view of the matter ultimate result of this money suit is as clear as day light, such a suit should be buried at its inception so that no further time is consumed in a fruitless litigation. Mr. Bikash Paul to strengthen his submissions has relied on the decisions reported in 45 DLR (AD) 31, 11 BLD 315, 10 BLT 39, 11 BLD 312, 43 DLR 242, 53 DLR(AD) 12 and 55 DLR 211.

10. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for both the sides and perused the plaint of the suit along with other materials on record including the agreement Between the parties as well as the impugned judgment and decree.

11. On scrutiny of the record, it appears that the plaintiff-appellants filed Money suit No. 79 of 2013 against the defendant-respondents claiming an amount of Taka 10,95,61,094 and the defendant-respondent Nos.l-9 entered appearance in the suit and filed written statement on 16-4-2014 and thereafter, on 17-9-2014 filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint on the ground that the plaintiffs without referring the matter to Arbitration as per Clause 25 of the agreement filed the instant suit and in that view of the matter the suit is impliedly barred by section 7 of the Arbitration Act. It also appears that the trial Court allowed the prayer for rejection of the plaint on the findings that the plaintiffs without referring the matter to arbitration as per Clause 25 of the agreement filed the suit and the plaintiffs earlier on the similar type dispute filed writ petition and according to direction given in the writ petition the defendants paid all outstanding dues to the plaintiffs.

12. We have gone through the Writ Petition No. 2871 of 2010 and the plaint of the instant suit and it appears that the subject matter of the earlier writ petition and the instant suit are not same inasmuch as the writ petition was filed praying for direction, to the Government of Bangladesh, represented by its Secretary Ministry of Communication, Bangladesh Secretariat, Ramna, Dhaka and others to make payment to the petitioners immediately for construction/development works done by the plaintiffs under different work orders and the instant money suit was filed by the plaintiffs claiming compensation amounting to Taka 10,95,61,094. Therefore, we find no reason accept the plea of res-judicata as taken in application under Order VII, rule 11 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection o f the plaint. Further, from a plain reading of the plaint it does not appear that the plaintiffs failed to disclose any cause of action for the suit.

13. Now coming to the 2nd question, it appears that in this case the defendant respondents entered appearance in the suit and filed written statement on 16-4-2014 and thereafter, they filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint on 17-9-2014 on the ground that the plaintiffs without referring the dispute to Arbitration as per clause 25 of the agreement, filed the suit and, as such„ the suit is barred by section 7 of the Arbitration Act.

14. In approaching the controversy it will be profitable to notice the provision contained in section 10 of the Arbitration Act, which is quoted hereunder:

"10. Arbitrability of the dispute—(1) Where any party to an arbitration agreement or any person claiming under him commences any legal proceedings against any other party to the agreement or any person claiming under him in respect of any matter agreed to be referred to arbitration, any party to such legal proceedings may, at any time before filing a written statement, apply to the Court before which proceedings are pending to refer the matter to arbitration.

(2) Thereupon, the Court shall, if it is satisfied that an arbitration agreement exists, refer the parties to arbitration and stay the proceedings, unless the Court finds that the arbitration agreement is void, inoperative or is incapable of determination by arbitration.

(3) Notwithstanding that an application has been made under sub-section (1) and that the issue is pending before the judicial authority, an arbitration may be commenced or continued and an arbitral award made."

15. A reading of the above provision set out above shows that any party of the agreement, may, at any time before filing a written statement, apply to the Court before which the proceeding is pending to refer the matter to arbitration but in this case we have already noticed that admittedly the defendants without applying to the Court before which the proceeding is pending to refer the matter to arbitration filed a written statement on 16-4-2014 and thereafter, filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint on 17-9-2014. Our view is, therefore, that in the facts and circumstances of the case and law bearing on the subject the application filed by the defendants was incompetent and misconceived as well inasmuch as admittedly the defendants without applying to the Court before which the proceeding is pending to refer the matter to arbitration filed a writ-ten statement on 16-4-2014 and thereafter, filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint on 11-9-2014.

16. Now, it remains for us to consider that whether the suit was barred by section 7 of the Arbitration Act.

<u>17. In the case of Bangladesh Water Development Board vs Contractor, Manu Barrage reported in 53 DLR 200, it has been held as follows:-</u>

<u>"The plaintiff instituted the suit. The defendant did not raise any objection to the institution of the suit. Rather, the defendant appeared in the suit, filed written statement and contested. After the final decision in the suit and in this appeal therefrom, it is very difficult for us to appreciate the submissions of Mr Rafiqur Rahman that in view of the arbitration agreement having remained alive, the suit is not maintainable. Moreover, we find no such provisions in the Act barring the suit on the ground of existence of an arbitration agreement. We find only one bar against a suit under section 32 of the Act, "no suit shall be on any ground whatsoever for a decision upon the existence, effect or validity of an arbitration agreement or award. The decision reported in 17 DLR (SC) 404 relied by Mr Rafiqur Rahman does not help him either. So, the submission of Mr Rafiqur Rahman on the issue of maintainability has no substance."</u>

18. Mr Aminul Islam, however, upon refer-ring to the agreement/contract submits that admittedly after completion of the construction/development work under agreement, the plaintiff-appellants filed the instant money suit claiming an amount of Taka 10,95,61,094 which does not fall within the ambit of said clause inasmuch as clause 25 of the agreement does not disclose anything with regard to payment of damage or compensation.

<u>19. In the given facts and circumstances of the case and the decision of the highest Court as cited above as well as the above submission of the learned Advocate for the appellants, we have no hesitation to hold that there is no legal scope to allow the application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint on the ground that the suit is barred by section 7 of the Arbitration Act. To decide the truth of the matter evidence is necessary which can be available only in the course of trial of the suit. The plea of implied bar should ordinarily be decided on evidence.</u>

20. It is indeed unfortunate that the learned joint district judge did not at all consider all these aspects of the case both on law and fact in deciding an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint and non-consideration of the same has caused a great miscarriage of justice. We are therefore of the opinion that the judgment and decree of the joint district judge is totally unsatisfactory and the same suffers from various error.

21. Here it may further be mentioned that the cases relied upon by the respondents have also so manner of application in the facts and circumstances of the case as the facts of the instant case are quite distinguishable from the facts of those cases.

22. In view of our discussions made in the foregoing paragraphs it is by now clear that the instant appeal must succeed.

23. In the result the appeal is allowed without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and decree dated 28-10-2014 (decree signed on 30-10-2014) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Money Suit No. 79 of 2013 rejecting the plaint is set-aside. The learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka is, however, directed to proceed with the suit expeditiously in accordance with law.

Let a copy of this judgment along with lower Court's record be sent down at once.

End.

lawyer:
Dr Naim Ahmed, Advocate-For the Petitioner in Writ Petition No. 5396 of 2008. 
Md. Emdadul Haque kazi, Advocate-For the Petitioner in Writ Petition No. 5564 of 2008. 
Md Ramzan Ali Sikder with Md Motahar Hossain and Mudassir Hossain, Advocates-For the Respondent No. 1 in Writ Petition Nos. 5396 of 2008 and 5564 of 2008.
parties:
Nazma Parveen & another ----- Petitioners
Vs
Lalmatia Mohila College and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Moyeenul Islam Chowdhury J : As the same question of laws and facts are involved in writ Petition No. 5396 of 2008 and 5564 of 2008, they have been heard together and are disposed of by this consolidated judgment.

2. In the Writ Petitions, Rule 8 Nisi were issued calling upon the respondent Nos. 1-2 to show cause as to why the decision of the respondent No.2 in its 115th meeting dated 29-4-2008 and Memo Nos. N/3-13370(5-1) and N/3-13371(5-1) both dated 14-5-2008 issued by the respondent No. 1 terminating the petitioners from the posts of Lecturers (ad hoc) in the Departments of History and Psychology of Lalmatia Mohila College, Dhaka should not be declared to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

3. The case of the petitioners, as set out in the Writ Petitions, in short, is as follows:—

The petitioners are law-abiding citizens of Bangladesh. They have good academic background. The petitioner of the Writ Petition No. 5396 of 2008, namely Nazma Parveen was appointed as a Lecturer in the Department of History of Lalmatia Mohila Collage, Dhaka on ad hoc basis for 6(six) months by Memo No. Ga /3-8038(7-1) dated 8-4-2004. Subsequently by Memo. No. Ga/3-8671(5-1) dated 9-11-2004, her service was extended on ad hoc basis until further orders. The petitioner of the other Writ Petition (Writ Petition No. 5564 of 2008) Roksana Munni was appointed as a part-time Lecturer in the Department of Psychology of the collage by Memo No. N/3-10585(5-1) dated 17-11-2005 under certain stipulations. Afterwards, she was appointed as a Lecturer in that department on ad hoc basis by Memo No. N/3-11814(5-1) dated 11-1-2007. Anyway, on their appointments both the petitioners had been discharging their respective duties honestly, sincerely and faithfully. But none the less, on 29-4-2008 the Governing Body of Lalmatia Mohila Collage, Dhaka (respondent No.2) in its 115th meeting discussed that as the number of students in the Departments of History and Psychology and some other Departments of the college was very meager, there was no requirement for retention of any ad hoc teacher therein and accordingly a decision was taken in the said meeting to terminate the petitioners and others by giving 3(three) months prior notice to them. Thereafter pursuant to the decision of the Governing Body of the college taken in its 115th meeting the petitioners were terminated from the service of the college by the impugned Memo Nos. N/3-13370(5-1) and N/3-13371 (5-1) both dated 14-5-2008 to be effective on and from 14-8-2008. The terminations of the petitioners from the service of Lalmatia Mohila College, Dhaka are without lawful authority and of no legal effect.

4. The respondent No. 1 in both the Writ Petitions has contested the Rules by filing Affidavits-in-Opposition. Its case, as set out therein, in brief, runs as follows:—

It is true that the petitioner of the Writ Petition No. 5396 of 2008 Nazma Parveen was appointed as a Lecturer in the Department of History of Lalmatia Mohila College, Dhaka on ad hoc basis. It is also true that the petitioner of the Writ Petition No. 5564 of 2008 Roksana Munni was initially appointed as a part-time Lecturer in the Department of Psychology of the college; but subsequently she was appointed as a Lecturer in the self-same department on ad hoc basis. Both the petitioners were appointed as Lecturers in their respective departments because of political clout and wire-pulling. The provisions relating to recruitment of teachers in the college were thrown to the winds due to backstage manoeuvres. There are no provisions for appointment of any teacher in the college on ad hoc basis within the four corners of the জাতীয় বিশ্ববিদ্যালয় অধিভূক্ত বেসরকারী কলেজ শিক্ষকদের চাকুরীর শর্তাবলী রেগুলেশন, ১৯৯৪ (hereinafter referred appointments of the petitioners as Lecturers on ad hoc basis are illegal. As the number of students in various departments of the college was inadequate and because of financial constraint, the Governing Body of the college in its 115th meeting took a decision to terminate the petitioners and others with 3(three) months prior notice and accordingly by the impugned orders dated 14-5-2008, they were terminated from the service of the college with effect from 14-8-2008. The respondent No. 1 did not commit any illegality in terminating the petitioners from the service of the college. Their terminations are terminations simpliciter. From this point of view, no exception can be taken thereto. As such, the Rules are liable to be discharged with costs.

5. At the outset, Dr. Naim Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner of the Writ Petition No. 5396 of 2008, submits that admittedly the petitioner Nazma Parveen was an ad hoc appointee (Lecturer in the Department of History) vide Annexure-'A' dated 8-4-2004; but the provisions of the 2nd Proviso to Regulation 15 of the Regulations of 1994 were not complied with before her termination and in that view of the matter, her termination from service is clearly without lawful authority and of no legal effect.

6. Dr. Naim Ahmed, however, concedes that there is no provision for appointment of a teacher on ad hoc basis within the four corners of the Regulations of 1994, though there is a provision for appointment of a part time teacher within the meaning of Regulation 2(cha)

7. Dr. Naim Ahmed further concedes that the termination of the petitioner Nazma Parveen from the service of Lalmatia Mohila College, Dhaka is a termination simpliciter.

8. Mr. Md. Emdadul Haque Kazi, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner Roksana Munni of the Writ Petition No. 5564 of 2008, submits that initially she was appointed as a part time Lecturer in the Department of Psychology vide Annexure-'B' dated 17-11-2005 and subsequently she was appointed as a Lecturer in that department on ad hoc basis by Annexure-'D' dated 11-1-2007 and the termination of the petitioner Roksana Munni on the score of inadequate number of students in the Department of Psychology and in view of the financial stringency of the college authority cannot be sustainable in law particularly when efforts were underway to appoint more teachers in various departments of the college.

9. Mr. Md. Emdadul Haque Kazi also submits that the impugned order of termination of the petitioner Roksana Munni is bad in law in any view of the matter.

10. On the other hand, Mr. Md. Ramzan Ali Sikder, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No.1 in both the Writ Petitions, submits that admittedly the petitioners were appointed on ad hoc basis as Lecturers in the Departments of History and Psychology of Lalmatia Mohila College, Dhaka and their terminations are terminations simpliciter and that being so, Lalmatia Mohila College being a private college is not amenable to the Writ jurisdiction of the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution and given this scenario, the petitioners have no locus standi to file the Writ petitions.

11. Mr. Md. Ramzan Ali Sikder further submits that it is an indisputable fact that the Principal of Lalmatia Mohila College is not performing any function in connection with the affairs of the Republic or of any local authority and in this perspective, the petitioners have no standing at all.

12. Mr. Md. Ramzan Ali Sikder also submits that the petitioners were admittedly appointed on ad hoc basis and they were never included in the Monthly Pay order (MPO) and their relationship with the college authority was that of master and servant and this being the panorama, the master cannot be forced to retain service of the servant and the remedy of the petitioners, if any, lies in a suit for damages in the competent Civil Court.

13. Mr. Md. Ramzan Ali Sikder next submits that there was a flagrant contravention of the provisions of Regulation 5 of the Regulations of 1994 in the matter of appointment of the petitioners and as there is no provision whatsoever for their appointments on ad hoc basis, they were rightly terminated from the service of Lalmatia Mohila College under Section 16 of the General Clauses Act.

14. In support of the above submissions, Mr. Md. Ramzan Ali Sikder has drawn our attention to the decisions in the cases of Khorshed Alam, Managing Director of Spark Engineering & Construction Ltd vs Ministry of Commerce. Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, Bangladesh Secretariat, 47 DLR (HCD) 209; Din Mohammad vs Government of Bangladesh, 14 BLD (AD) 142; Alauddin Sikder (Md) vs Bangladesh, 56 DLR (AD) 130; Messrs Malik ,& Haq vs Md Shamsul Islam Chowdhury, 13 DLR (SC) 228; Cholera Research Laboratory, Dhaka vs Md. Mozammel Huq, 25 DLR 260 and Jamal Uddin vs Kashem Bahumukhi High School, 56 DLR (HCD) 474.

15. We have heard the submissions of Dr. Naim Ahmed and Mr. Md. Emdadul Haque Kazi and the counter-submissions of Mr. Md. Ramzan Ali Sikder, perused the Writ Petitions. Affidavits-in-Opposition and relevant Annexures annexed thereto.

16. It is admitted that the petitioner of the Writ Petition No. 5396 of 2008 Nazma Parveen was initially appointed as a Lecturer in the Department of History of Lalmatia Mohila College for 6(six) months on ad hoc basis vide Annexure' A' dated 8-4-2004. It is further admitted that subsequently by Memo No. Ga/3-8671(5-1) dated 9-11-2004, her service was extended on ad hoc basis until further orders. Again, it is undisputed that the petitioner of the Writ Petition No. 5564 of 2008 Roksana Munni was initially appointed as a part time Lecturer in the Department of Psychology on 17-11-2005. Undeniably, she was appointed on ad hoc basis as a Lecturer in the self-same department by Memo No. N/3-11814(5-1) dated 11-1-2007. However, by the impugned orders dated 14-5-2008 the petitioners were terminated from the service of the college. The orders of termination are under challenge in the Writ Petitions.

17. The moot question before us is whether the petitioners have any locus standi to file the Writ petitions. It goes without saying that Lalmatia Mohila College is a non-Government (private) college. There is no gainsaying the fact that the Principal of this private college is not performing any function in connection with the affairs of the Republic or of a local authority.

18. In this regard, a reference may be made to the definition of 'Local Authority' as given in Section 3 (28) of the General Act of 1897. Section 3 (28) of the Act is reproduced below:—

"Local Authority—'Local authority' shall mean and include a Paurashava, Zilla Board, Union Panchayat, Board of Trustees of a port or other authority legally entitled to, or entrusted by the Government with the control or management of a municipal or local fund, or any corporation or other body or authority constituted or established by the Government under any law."

19. Having regard to the definition of 'Local Authority' in the General Clauses Act (quoted above), a non-Government college cannot be held to be a local authority inasmuch as, it has not been constituted or established by the Government under any law. Both Dr Naim Ahmed and Mr Md Emdadul Haque Kazi candidly concede that Lalmatia College being a private college is not a local authority within the meaning of Section 3 (28) of the 'General Clauses Act. It is a truism that the Principal of Lalmatia Mohila College is not performing any function in connection with the affairs of the Republic. As the college is not a local authority within the meaning of Section 3 (28) of the General Clauses Act and as it is not performing any function in connection with the affairs of the Republic, the same is not amenable to the writ jurisdiction of the High Court, Division under Article 102 of the Constitution, On this point, our view is buttressed up by the decision in the case of Mofizul Huq vs Mofizur Rahman reported in 49 DLR(AD) 38. In that decision, our Appellate Division has clearly, categorically and unambiguously held that a recognized non-Government school is neither a statutory body nor a local authority within the meaning of the General Clauses Act. So obviously Lalmatia Mohila College is neither a statutory body nor a local authority as per the General Clauses Act.

20. The decisions in the cases of Khorshed Alam, Managing Director of Spark Engineering & Construction Ltd vs Ministry of Commerce, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, Bangladesh Secretarial, 47 DLR 209; Din Mohammad vs Government of Bangladesh, 14 BLD (AD) 142 and Alauddin Sikder vs Bangladesh, 56 DLR (AD) 130 relied on by Mr Md Ramzan Ali Sikder are not exactly on the point we are dealing with.

21. In 'the decision in the case of Messrs Malik & Haq vs Md Shamsul Islam Chowdhury reported in 13 DLR (SC) 228 referred to by Mr Md Ramzan Ali Sikder, it has been held that the master cannot be forced to retain the service of a servant against his will, but he may be liable to pay damages, if any, to the servant for breach of contract.

22. In the decision in the case Cholera Research Laboratory, Dacca vs Md Mozammel Huq reported in 25 DLR 260 adverted to by Mr Md Ramzan Ali Sikder, it has been held in paragraph 12.

"12. From the above mentioned decisions, it appears that the law relating to a dismissed employee other than Government Servant is now settled. Such a case is covered by the law of Master and Servant. In the case reported in 21 DLR (SC) 365, a dismissed employee of Eastern Mercantile Bank Ltd instituted a suit for declaration that the order terminating his service was null and void. In that case, the plaintiff complained of violation of the regulation of the Bank in terminating his service. The learned Judges of the Supreme Court referred to the earlier decision of the Court reported in 13 DLR (SC) 228 and reiterated the view taken therein. It has been held that since the respondent's services were not regulated by any legal instrument, it could not be said that the declaration asked for by him was in relation to any legal character. It was held that such a suit not being in relation to any legal character is not maintainable under Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. It was further held that in such cases, the law of Master and Servant is applicable and the remedy of an aggrieved person lies in a suit for damages only. On careful examination of the said decision; it appears that the present case is fully covered by the decision."

23. In the case of Jamal Uddin vs Mir Kashem Bahumukhi High School, reported in 56 DLR 474, it has been held that when the service of the petitioner is governed by the rules of Master and Servant, the Master cannot be forced to accept the service of the Servant.

24. As already observed, the petitioners were appointed on ad hoc basis in the Departments of History and Psychology of Lalmatia Mohila College, Dhaka. Admittedly there are no provisions whatsoever for appointment of the petitioners on ad hoc .basis within the four corners of the Regulations of 1994. This being the picture, their service is not regulated by any legal instrument. In such a posture of things, it leaves no room for doubt that the relationship between Lalmatia Mohila College Authority and the petitioners is that of Master and Servant, to all intents and purposes.

25. From the foregoing discussions and in view of the facts and circumstances of the case, we have no hesitation in holding that the petitioners have no locus standi at all to file the Writ Petitions. Consequently, on this score alone, the Rules are liable to be discharged.

26. As we have found that the petitioners have no standing, we refrain from making any observation as to the merit of the case.

<u>27. Regard being had to the facts and circumstances of the case, it transpires that the petitioners filed the instant Writ Petitioners knowing full well that they had no locus standi to do so. As we see it, they should be saddled with some costs in that Lalmatia Mohila College Authority had to contest the Rules out of the coffers of the college. Furthermore, the awarding of costs will serve as a deterrent to others so that they will feel disinclined to come up with frivolous and vexatious Writ Petitions in future.</u>

<u>Accordingly, the Rules are discharged on the ground of incompetency of the Writ Petitions. Each petitioner is directed to pay costs of Taka 5,000 (five thousand) only to the respondent No. 1 within 30 (thirty) days from date, failing which, the costs shall be realized from her through the process of the Court.</u>

End.

full_judgment:
Obaidul Hassan J : In an application under Article 102(2)(a)(ii) of the Constitution by the petitioner the Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned orders passed by the Bangladesh Power Development Board and Communicated by the Respondent no. 7 under his Memo No. 160-PBD (Ta: Sri)/3/A-15/2006 dated 28-11-2007(Annexure J) and the Memo No. 66-PDB (Ta: Sri)/3/A-15/2006 dated 07-2-2008 (Annexure K) imposing penalty upon the petitioner after submission of inquiry report by the Inquiry Officer with findings that the charges brought against the petitioner had not been established should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. The relevant facts for disposal of the rule are that, the petitioner was appointed as Assistant Engineer in Bangladesh Power Development  Board (PDB) and he joined in service on 06-9-1986 in the Distribution Division, Noakhali, Bangladesh Power Development Board, Noakhali. He was ultimately promoted to the post of Sub Divisional Engineer and was posted to Sales and Distribution Division, Mohora Chittagong on 15-11-2001. During his service the petitioner was transferred to Bhairab Electric Supply as Resident Engineer (Sub Divisional Engineer) and he joined there on 07-12-2004 and thereafter he was transferred to 90 MW Combined Circle Power Plant, Fenchugonj, Shlhet on 31-1-2006. While he was serving in that station the authority by then letter No. 358-PDB (Ta: Sri)/3 /A-15 / 2006 dated 19-11-2006 asked the petitioner to show cause as to why disciplinary action should not be taken against him for the charges of negligence in his duties, misconduct and corruption. After receiving the said show cause notice the petitioner gave his reply with explanation on 02-12-2006. In reply he denied the charge brought against him and stated that no irregularity was committed by him. He further stated that no consumer was harassed by the petitioner and he properly prepared the bills. He enclosed some official documents with his explanation. Thereafter the concerned authority framed charges against the petitioner and by their letter No. 368-PDB (Ta: Sri)/3 /A-15 /2006 dated 20-12-2006 informed the petitioner that the authority had appointed one Mr. Md. Jamal Ullah, Superintending Engineer, Auditing Unit Power Development Board (PDB), Dhaka as the Enquiry Officer for holding inquiry of charges brought against the petitioner. The petitioner was further directed to show cause as to why he should not be punished under Rule 138(a)(c) of the Bangladesh Power Development Board, Employees Service Rule 1982 (hereinafter called PDB Service Rule 1982). After receiving the charge-sheet dated 20-12-1006 the petitioner submitted his reply dated 27-12-2006 and denied the charges brought against him and stated that the penal bill was not done under his signature. No irregularity was committed by him informing the enquiry committee, the person who consumed electricity was convicted by the competent court. He gave some papers with his reply.

3. Thereafter on 15-1-2006 the Respondent No.7 by his letter No. 10 PDB (Ta: Sri)/3/A-15/2006 directed the petitioner to explain the causes in respect of amended bills and accordingly the petitioner gave his explanation on- 20-11-1007. Thereafter the enquiry officer informed the petitioner to remain present before him with necessary papers and accordingly the petitioner and the prosecutor for Bangladesh Power Development Board was present before the enquiry officer. After hearing both sides the enquiry officer submitted his inquiry report on 15-1-2007 Thereafter the concerned authority by their letter dated 15-2-2007 wanted an opinion and recommendation from the Inquiry Officer in respect of inquiry report filed by him on 15-1-2007. Accordingly the enquiry officer submitted his opinion and recommendation on 08-3-2007. Thereafter on 03-6-2007 the concerned authority by filing another letter No. 43-PDB (Ta: Sri)/3/A-15/2006 asked the petitioner to show cause as to why he should not be punished under Section 139(1)(b) of the PDB Service Rules 1982 withholding 5(five) yearly increments for 1 year each. The petitioner on 15-6-2007 gave his reply showing his innocence. Thereafter the concerned authority (the respondents; by their letter No. 160-PDB (Ta: Sri)/3/A15/2006 dated 28-11-2007 imposed penalty upon the petitioner under Section 139(1)(b) of the PDB Service Rules 1982 withholding 5(five) yearly increments one for each year and for which no arrear would be paid.

4. The petitioner being aggrieved with the said penalty filed a review application to the Power Development Board on 17-12-2007 through proper channel with a prayer for withdrawal of the penalty. The Reviewing authority did not consider the prayer for review and informed the petitioner on 07-2-2008 accordingly. Thereafter the petitioner came before this court challenging the letter No. 160- PDB (Ta: Sri)/3/A-15/2006 dated 28-11-2007 by which punishment was awarded to him and obtained the instant rule.

5. Mr Tufailur Rahman, learned Advocate entered appearance on behalf of the Respondent Nos. 2, 3 and 8 along with Mst. Umme Salma, Advocate. He controverted the material statements made by the petitioner in the writ petition and stated that while the petitioner was posted in Bhairab Electricity apply be committed serious irregularities in issuing the penal bill dated 30-7-200 to the Bhairab Ferry hat Fish Samity, in connection with the issuance of bill of Taka 3,26,839 for using numberless meter by the aforesaid samity. Accordingly he was issued with the show cause notice dated 19-11-2006 containing specific allegations. The respondent also stated that since the reply of the petitioner to the show cause notice was not satisfactory, an enquiry committee was constituted to enquire into the charges brought against the petitioner. The said committee held inquiry in compliance of legal formalities. The petitioner was given opportunity to rebut the charges brought against him. The enquiry officer duly submitted his inquiry report. It is also stated by .the respondents that on 15-2-2007 the enquiry officer was asked to give his opinion regarding certain specific mentioned in the said letter after examining the reply of the petitioner and the records of the case. In pursuance to the inquiry report, the opinion; the recommendation, and the allegations against the petitioner being of serious nature a second show cause notice was also served upon him. Since his reply was found to be not satisfactory, he was awarded punishment in accordance with the PDB Service Rules 1982. The respondents also stated that the review application was duly considered but as there was no substance in the review application it was rejected.

6. Mr Md. Abdul Haque, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the enquiry officer after holding the enquiry observing all the legal formalities found the petitioner not guilty of the charges brought against him by the PDB authority and accordingly submitted his report. The respondents without considering the inquiry report inflicted the punishment on the petitioner which is not sustainable in law. He further submits that the respondents did not have any materials in their hands other than the inquiry report to establish the charges against the petitioner and, as such, the impugned order is illegal and has been issued, without lawful authority. Mr. Abdul Haque further submits that in inflicting the punishment upon the petitioner the respondents did not have any independent and different opinion other than the opinion of the enquiry officer and, as such, there was no any basis for inflicting punishment upon the petitioner. The respondents have done it according to their own whims and, as such, the impugned order dated 28-11-2007 is liable to be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. He further submits that the punishment has been inflicted upon the petitioner without following the provision of rule 143(4) of the PDB Service Rules 1982, the proceeding was initiated after expiration of specific period of 3(three) months and, as such, the whole proceeding was illegal and, as such, the impugned order is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority.

7. Mr Tufailur Rahman, the learned Advocate for the respondent Nos. 2, 3 and 8 submits that the authority has the right to impose any penalty upon an employee for misconduct negligence or for other irregularities considering the inquiry report. In this case the Inquiry report was not satisfactory, after going through the records and considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the inquiry report itself, the respondents inflicted the punishment upon the petitioner because the charges were grave in nature. Mr. Tufailur Rahman further submits that as per rule 143(4) of the PDB Service Rules 1982) the authority has the right to impose any upon any employee for charges of misconduct and irregularities. Considering the reply of the petitioner to the show cause notices, the report of the enquiry officer and the facts and circumstances of the case the authority has imposed the penalty which was justified. However, Mr Tufailur Rahman candidly submits that in the impugned order dated 28-11-2007 it has not been mentioned how the authority was satisfied to impose the penalty upon the petitioner. No reasoning whatsoever was given in the impugned order.

8. We have gone through the writ petition along with Annexures, Affidavit-in-opposition field by the respondents, supplementary affidavit on behalf of the petitioner and relevant laws referred by the parties. It appears that the petitioner was charged with some particular allegations and he gave reply those allegation. Thereafter a proper inquiry was held and it was found that the petitioner was not guilty of the charges brought against him. It also appears that vide Annexure-F the enquiry officer gave his decision against each and every allegation brought against the petitioner, saying that the allegations were unfounded. From Annexure-G it appears that the enquiry officer was asked to give his opinion, accordingly he opined that it was not found that the petitioner was involved with the offence mentioned in the charges. We have gone though the decisions given by the authority imposing punishment upon the petitioner, the authority said that:—

“যেহেতু বোর্ড অভিযুক্ত জনাব মোঃ আবুল কালাম আজাদ, সাবেক আবাসিক প্রকৌশলী, ভৈরব বিদ্যুৎ সরবরাহ, বিউবো, ভৈরব, কিশোরগঞ্জ বর্তমানে নির্বাহী প্রকৌশলী (চলতি দায়িত্ব), ৯০ মেঃওঃ ফেঞ্চুগঞ্জ বিদ্যুৎ কেন্দ্র, বিউবো, সিলেট এর লিখিত আত্নপক্ষ সমর্থনমূলক জবাব, তদন্ত প্রতিবেদন, তদন্তকারী কর্মকর্তার ফাইন্ডিংস ও আনুষাঙ্গিক কাগজপত্র পর্যালোচনা ও বিশ্লেষন পূর্বক তাকে ২০-১২-২০০৬ ইং তারিখের স্মারকে বর্ণিত অভিযোগে দোষী সাব্যস্থ করে বিউবো চাকুরী বিধির ১৩৯(১) (বি) ধারা মোতাবেক তার পরবর্তী ৫ (পাঁচ) টি বার্ষিক বেতন বৃদ্ধি প্রতিটি ০১ (এক) বছরের জন্য স্থগিত (যার কোন বকেয়া পাবেন না) রাখার শাস্তি কেন আরোপ করা হবে না সে বিষয়ে দপ্তরাদেশ নং ৫৩-বিউবো (তঃশৃঃ)/৩/এ-১৫/২০০৬ তারিখ ৩/৬/২০০৭ ইং মোতাবেক তাঁকে দ্বিতীয় কারন দর্শানোর নোটিশ প্রমানসহ আনুষ্ঠানিক তদন্ত প্রতিবেদনের পর্যালোচনা সংশোধন করেন; এবং

যেহেতু, অভিযুক্ত জনাব মোঃ আবুল কালাম আজাদ, সাবেক আবাসিক প্রকৌশলী, ভৈরব বিদ্যুৎ সরবরাহ, বিউবো, ভৈরব, কিশোরগঞ্জ বর্তমানে-নির্বাহী প্রকৌশলী (চলতি দায়িত্ব) ৯০ মেঃওঃ ফেঞ্চুগঞ্জ বিদ্যুৎ কেন্দ্র, বিউবো, সিলেট এর লিখিত দ্বিতীয় কারণ দর্শানোর জবাব ও তৎসংগে সংযুক্ত সংযোজনী পর্যালোচনায় ও বিশ্লেষনে ভিন্নতর সিদ্ধান্ত প্রনয়নে যৌক্তিক কোন উপাদান পাওয়া না যাওয়ায় অর্থাৎ অসাধুতা তঞ্চকতা ও জালিয়াতি জনিত কর্তব্যে অবহেলা ও অসদাচরন এর অভিযোগ সন্দেহাতীতভাবে প্রমানিত হওয়ায় বোর্ডে দোষী সাব্যস্ত করতঃ বিউবো চাকুরী বিধির ১৩৯(১)(বি) ধারা মোতাবেক তার পরবর্তী ৫(পাচ) টি বার্ষিক বেতন বৃদ্ধি প্রতিটি ০১(এক) বছরের জন্য স্থগিত (যার কোন বকেয়া পাবেন না) রাখার শাস্তি আরোপের সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহন করেন।”

সেহেতু, এক্ষনে জনাব মোঃ আবুল কালাম আজাদ, সাবেক-আবাসিক প্রকৌশলী, ভৈরব বিদ্যুৎ সরবরাহ, বিউবো, ভৈরব, কিশোরগঞ্জ বর্তমানে-নির্বাহী প্রকৌশলী (চলতি দায়িত্‌), ৯০ মেঃ ওঃ ফেঞ্চুগঞ্জ বিদ্যুৎ কেন্দ্র বিউবো, সিলেট এর বিরুদ্ধে অসাধুতা, তঞ্চকতা ও জালিয়তি জনিত কর্তব্যে

অবহেলা ও অসদাচরন এর অভিযোগ সন্দেহাতীতভাবে প্রমাণিত হওয়ায় বোর্ডে দোষী সাব্যস্ত করতঃ বিউবো চাকুরী বিধির ১৩৯১) (বি) ধারা মোতাবেক তার পরবর্তী ৫(পাচ) টি বার্ষিক বেতন বৃদ্ধি প্রতিটি ০১ (এক) বছরের জন্য স্থগিত (যার কোন বকেয়া পাবেন না) রাখার শাস্তি আরোপ করা হল-যা অবিলঙ্গে কার্যকর হবে ।”

9. It appears from the impugned order that the authority after considering the inquiry report and other papers had imposed the penalty, but it did not give any reason why the inquiry report should not be believed and what satisfaction it had in imposing the penalty upon the petitioner. From the available papers and records we do not find any tangible evidence against the petitioner for making him responsible for the charges brought against him. If the enquiry officer had not held the inquiry in a proper manner the duty of the authority was to change the enquiry officer and to inquire into the matter afresh, but without doing so they have imposed the penalty without giving any reason. In our view it has been done whimsically.

10. Mr. Md. Abdul Haque the learned Advocate referred one unreported judgment passed in Writ Petition No. 4861 of 2007 along with Writ Petition No. 2579 of 2008. By a single judgment the two writ petitions were disposed of. The petitioners of those two writ petitions were similarly situated persons as the petitioner. In the judgment their Lordships held that statutory powers given for disciplinary action must be exercised in such a way so that not only the delinquent employee could understand why he was punished but also any prudent person may find the reasons justifying the action taken. This kind of disposal of disciplinary proceeding was always deprecated but without any result." In the present case it is not also understandable for what reason the petitioner was punished. Since from the inquiry report it was found that each and every allegation brought against the writ petitioner was not proved the authority was not justified in imposing any penalty without giving its own reason.

11. Rule 143(4) has given an ample power to the authority to impose any penalty upon the person against whom the charges have been brought even ignoring the inquire report. Context of which runs as follows:

"143. Inquiry procedure in cases of negligence, inefficiency, misconduct and corruption—

(4) The authority competent to impose the penalty shall consider the written statement submitted by the employee in his defence, the report of the Enquiry Officer and other circumstances, if any, and impose such penalty as it may deem proper in the circumstances of the case;

Provided that before imposition of penalty of compulsory retirement, dismissal, removal or reduction to a lower post, the delinquent employee shall be given second opportunity to show cause against the penalty proposed to be imposed. The decision of the authority shall be communicated by an order in writing to the employee concerned. The proceedings under this rule shall be completed within three months from the date of framing charge against an employee."

<u>12. It appears that the report of the enquiry officer is not binding upon the Board. But such power to in pose penal sanction could only be exercised despite the reports of enquiry on the basis of certain conclusion based on evidence that the petitioner was guilty. The authority must come to a conclusion on the basis of at least some proof. In the impugned orders, we find, exercise of the powers imposing penalty without any basis whatsoever. Similarly, disposal of the review petition which is the last forum for decisions on facts and law by one sentence cannot be appreciated. Such kind of disposal of appeal/revision must be held to be not in accordance with law, lacking application of mind.</u>

13. In our opinion, there must be a reason and factual basis for imposing any penalty upon the delinquent. In this case any reason in imposing penalty against the petitioner was totally absent.

14. In the facts and circumstances stated above, considering the papers and submissions of both sides we are of the view that the impugned order of punishment contained in Memo No. 160- PUB (Ta: Sri)/3/A15 /2006 dated 28-11-2007 (Annexure J) has been issued without lawful authority and in an unlawful manner.

There is merit in the Rule and accordingly the Rule is made absolute. However there shall be no order as to costs.

End.

AKM Shahidul Islam, Advocate-on-Record—For Respondent No.6. (In CP No. 1159 of 2011)
